newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 still vulnerable to further declines.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 still vulnerable to further declines.

text.p: The UK equity market remains vulnerable to further losses next week amid growing perceptions that the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again in May, dealers and economists said on Friday.
They said events on Wall Street would continue to set the tone for London even with Britain in the throes of an election campaign.
"The market also has to adjust to the expectation that U.S. corporate profits are going to be squeezed as a result of higher rates," said economist Nick Stamenkovic of DKB International.
"And with bond yields rising, equity markets will continue to struggle," he added.
The U.S. employment report for March reinforced the view that the Fed's move to tighten last week was not a one-off measure, they said.
While U.S. non-farm payrolls rose by a slightly smaller-than-expected 175,000 in March, hourly earnings rose by a higher-than-expected $0.05.
"My guess is that (the increase in hourly earnings) is consistent with the view that the Fed will move (to raise interest rates) on May 20," said Neil MacKinnon, chief economist at Citibank.
MacKinnon said he expected the Fed funds rate to be lifted to 6-1/4 percent by the end of the year.
Next week's U.S. retail sales and producer price index (PPI), due on Friday, are likely to be the focus, although dealers and economists said they didn't expect the figures to help stock markets.
They said U.S. retail sales are likely to confirm the U.S. economy is expanding at a healthy pace and the U.S. PPI is unlikely to show that inflation has heated up.
"There's nothing to suggest that inflation is picking up strongly," said Stamenkovic. "But the inflation risk is on the upside."
Another focus for equity markets will come early in the week when Motorola Inc, a bellwether for the technology industry, publishes its first quarter results.
UK economic reports due next week include industrial production, manufacturing output, housing completions, housing starts and new construction orders.
RJB Mining Plc, Tesco Plc, Burmah Castrol Plc, RMC Group Plc and Tarmac Plc are scheduled to report their 1996 results.
Highland Distilleries Co Plc, Manchester United Plc and Smiths Industries Plc are due to report their interim results.
Other U.S. data due next week include consumer credit and wholesale inventories. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
